title: What to pack for a beach trip
summary: A full beach trip packing list with clothes, sun care, gear, and the essentials, plus the easy way to pay and stay connected abroad. Start.
body_markdown:
A day at the beach sounds simple enough: find a good spot, enjoy the water, soak up some sunshine and take a break from your usual routine. However, forgetting something as basic as sunscreen, a towel, or a change of clothes can make the experience less enjoyable. Whether you are heading to a nearby beach for the afternoon or planning a week-long seaside holiday, preparing what you need beforehand helps you make the most of your time.


For a beach trip, pack swimwear, a cover-up, sun hat, sunglasses, high-SPF sunscreen, sandals, a quick-dry towel, and a waterproof phone pouch. Add a reusable water bottle and a beach bag. For overseas trips, bring a card with no foreign fees and a travel eSIM for maps and bookings.


Putting together a beach trip packing list helps you organise your essentials without carrying unnecessary items. Think about how long you will be away, the activities you have planned and the weather at your destination. From beachwear and personal care products to travel documents and payment options, having everything organised makes travelling easier. This guide covers what to pack for a comfortable and enjoyable beach getaway.


### **Beach trip packing list: The essentials**


Planning a beach holiday means choosing suitable clothing and accessories while considering your destination, activities and budget, including Caribbean and Bahamas travel costs.


#### **Swimwear**


Pack at least two swimsuits so you always have a dry option while the other is drying. Choose comfortable swimwear suited to your planned activities, whether swimming, surfing or relaxing by the pool. A rash guard is also useful for additional sun protection, particularly if you intend to spend several hours in the water.


#### **Clothing**


Choose lightweight, breathable clothing such as cotton shirts, linen trousers, shorts and summer dresses. These are comfortable in warm weather and can be mixed and matched for different outings. Pack enough underwear and sleepwear for your stay, along with one or two outfits for dinners, sightseeing or evening activities.


#### **Footwear**


Bring comfortable flip-flops or sandals for walking on the beach and around your accommodation. Water shoes are useful for rocky shores, while casual trainers or flats work better for sightseeing and other activities. Choose versatile footwear that is comfortable, easy to clean and suitable for your itinerary.


#### **Cover-ups**


Pack a sarong, beach robe, kaftan or lightweight cover-up for when you leave the water. These are useful when visiting beachside restaurants, walking around a resort or relaxing outside the beach. Choose breathable fabrics that dry quickly and take up little luggage space. If the Bahamas is on your itinerary, researching[how much a trip to the Bahamas costs](http://grey.co/blog/trip-to-bahamas-cost) can help you plan your overall holiday budget.


## **Sun care and beach essentials**


Spending a day at the beach means preparing for more than just swimming and relaxing by the water. You will need protection from the sun, comfortable accessories for the sand and a few essentials for water activities. These items help you enjoy your time outdoors while staying protected and keeping your belongings safe.


#### **Sunscreen and sun protection**


Start with a broad-spectrum sunscreen of SPF 30 or higher to protect against UVA and UVB rays. Apply it before heading outdoors and reapply every two hours, especially after swimming or sweating. A wide-brimmed hat and UV-protective sunglasses provide additional protection, particularly when spending long hours under direct sunlight.


#### **Towels and beach accessories**


A quick-dry beach towel is useful for drying off after swimming or creating a comfortable spot on the sand. You can also bring a lightweight beach mat, reusable water bottle and spacious beach bag to keep your belongings organised. Choose accessories that are easy to carry and dry quickly.


#### **Waterproof pouches and snorkelling gear**


Protect your phone and other small valuables with a waterproof pouch, particularly when swimming or participating in water activities. If you plan to explore underwater, pack a snorkel, mask and fins, or check whether your destination offers equipment rentals.


Prepare the documents, payment options and technology you need to stay organised, spend conveniently and remain connected throughout your beach holiday.


## **Travel documents, payments and connectivity for your beach trip**


#### **Payment cards and cash**


Carry a payment card for hotel reservations, restaurant bills and other purchases, alongside some local currency for taxis, beach vendors and small transactions. Grey helps you manage cross-border payments,[hold foreign currency](https://grey.co/foreign-accounts) and[spend using a virtual card with no markup](http://grey.co/cards) on eligible transactions. Check applicable fees before departure.


#### **Travel documents**


Keep your passport, visa, flight tickets, accommodation details and travel insurance information somewhere secure but accessible. Save digital copies on your phone and keep physical copies of important documents as a backup. Having these details readily available makes airport checks, hotel check-ins and other travel arrangements easier to manage.


#### **eSIM and travel technology**


If you are visiting overseas beaches, consider getting a travel eSIM to access mobile data for maps, bookings and communication. Pack your phone charger, power bank and travel adapter, ensuring you can stay connected throughout your holiday. Check eSIM coverage and compatibility with your phone before travelling.


## **Beach packing checklist**


Use this beach packing checklist to organise your essentials before departure, keep track of what you have packed and avoid forgetting important items.


Item Why you need it


Swimwear For swimming, water activities and relaxing by the pool.


Sunscreen (SPF 30+) Protects your skin from harmful UV rays.


Sun hat Provides shade and protects your face from direct sunlight.


Sunglasses Protects your eyes from bright sunlight and glare.


Beach towel Helps you dry off after swimming or sunbathing.


Sandals Comfortable footwear for walking around the beach.


Cover-up Provides extra coverage when leaving the water.


Reusable water bottle Keeps you hydrated throughout the day.


Waterproof phone pouch Protects your phone from water and sand.


Travel documents Keeps your passport, tickets and bookings accessible.

## **Frequently asked questions about beach packing**


#### **1. What should I pack for a beach holiday?**


Pack swimwear, lightweight clothing, cover-ups, sandals, sunglasses, a sun hat and sunscreen. Include a quick-dry towel, reusable water bottle, waterproof phone pouch and toiletries. If you plan to participate in water activities, consider bringing snorkelling gear. Adjust your packing list based on your destination, planned activities and length of stay.


#### **2. What SPF should I bring to the beach?**


Choose a broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher to protect against UVA and UVB rays. If you plan to spend several hours swimming or outdoors, consider a water-resistant formula. Apply sunscreen before going outside and reapply every two hours, or more frequently after swimming, sweating or towel drying.


#### **3. What do I need for an overseas beach trip?**


For an overseas beach trip, pack your passport, visa, flight tickets, accommodation details and travel insurance documents. Bring a payment card, some local currency, suitable clothing, sunscreen and personal essentials. A travel eSIM, power bank and universal adapter will also help you stay connected and manage your travel arrangements.


#### **4. How many swimsuits should I pack for a beach holiday?**


Pack at least two swimsuits for a short beach holiday so you have a dry option while the other is drying. For longer stays, consider three or four, depending on your planned activities and access to laundry facilities. Choose comfortable options suitable for swimming, sunbathing and other water activities.


#### **5. What shoes should I wear on a beach holiday?**


Pack comfortable sandals or flip-flops for walking on the sand and around your accommodation. Water shoes are useful for rocky beaches, coral shores and water activities, while trainers or casual flats are better for sightseeing. Choose lightweight, versatile footwear that dries easily and suits your planned activities.


#### **6. How do I protect my belongings at the beach?**


Use a waterproof pouch for your phone and other small valuables, and keep your cash, cards and travel documents in a secure, separate bag. Avoid leaving expensive items unattended while swimming. If your accommodation offers lockers or secure storage, use them for passports, electronics and other important belongings.
